title: Stalk criterion for strict-local cohomology exchange
statement: For a qcqs morphism g : T ⟶ S, a sheaf F on T and degree q, the geometric stalk of the degree-q derived exchange at x is an isomorphism if and only if the induced pullback map on the cohomology of the corresponding strict henselization base-change square is bijective, for every compatible strict-local ring map a.

proof.text: Give the small strict-henselization rings their existing strictly henselian local structures. Evaluation factors through the surjective map onto the relative separable closure, then a field embedding, hence is local. The evaluation equation makes a local by isLocalHom_of_comp. Factor evaluation through the residue field using ResidueField.lift. The residue square follows from the evaluation equation by quotient extensionality. The structural pointed equations are strictHenselizationClosedLift_over.

Use Spec of the inverse smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso as each comparison to the full strict localization. The theorem smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso_toBase identifies their structural maps. Take the total spaces to be the two displayed products. Pullback cancellation constructs the cartesian square of the induced pullback.map with the projections to the strict-local bases. For the identity reparametrizations of the points, a private equality-elimination lemma transports the model isomorphism together with its structural composite; it is proved by substitution.

Apply exists_addEquiv_strictHenselization_abelian_stalkExchange to the flipped chosen pullback square, with both point fields equal to Ω and the two connecting field maps identities. This gives additive equivalences conjugating the original exchange stalk to exchange on the strict-local bases.

Apply exists_addEquiv_strictLocal_abelian_total_exchange to that strict-local cartesian square and the inverse image of F. Compose the additive equivalences and their intertwining equations. Replace α using its required equality to canonical exchange. An additive-group morphism is invertible exactly when its underlying function is bijective; bijectivity is unchanged by composition with either equivalence. This proves the claimed equivalence without new holes.
